exposure: Type of delivery (Caesarean section, vaginal delivery)
cohort: The participants were 178 consecutive infants examined at a paediatric chiropractic clinic between January 1, 2010 to December 31, 2010.
finding: Glenohumeral joint dysfunction was apparent in 73.6% of infants presenting to a paediatric chiropractic clinic, with significant positive linear correlation found between dysfunction and increasing birth weight in firstborns, and longer gestation length in females.
mod_finding: Prevalence of glenohumeral joint dysfunction was increased with Caesarean section (78.7%) compared to vaginal delivery (71.8%), though statistical significance for this association was not reached in the overall cohort analysis.
cross-section timing: Data was collated from January 1, 2010 to December 31, 2010.
birth_weight: Babies with birth weight >3.5kg and <3.5kg were included and compared.
gest_age: Gestational age was considered as 'longer gestation length' in relation to outcomes in females.
